digest.top_line: BEACON-HCC: 96.6% expert concordance vs 72.4% for BCLC 2025 across 29 cases, and EBRT/TARE finally sit at the allocation table.
digest.tldr: Hepatobiliary carries the day, and the RT-relevant point is structural rather than an effect size: BEACON-HCC is a Delphi allocation framework that names EBRT as a modality BCLC 2025 does not. Concordance was measured against the experts who wrote it, so this is consensus, not outcome.

sites.intro: One consensus framework, no outcome data: relevant to rad onc only insofar as it moves EBRT from omitted to allocable.

studies.name: BEACON-HCC
studies.tldr: Consensus HCC allocation framework: 96.6% expert concordance vs 72.4% for BCLC 2025 across 29 real-world cases.
details: 🔍 Modified Delphi, 20 North American experts (hepatology, med onc, surgery, radiology, rad onc), iterative discussion + voting
📊 Pilot: 29 real-world cases; expert decisions 96.6% concordant with BEACON-HCC, 72.4% with BCLC 2025
📐 EBRT and TARE named as incorporated modalities, alongside systemic-locoregional combinations
🔍 Allocation keyed to intrahepatic tumor burden, vascular invasion, and adverse tumor prognostic markers rather than stage alone
🔗 Positions against BCLC 2025, which does not carry EBRT as an allocation-level option in North American practice
⚠️ Concordance is between experts and a framework those experts helped write; not an outcome endpoint
⚠️ 29 cases is a pilot, and case selection is not described in source text
⚠️ Panel is heavily industry-conflicted (device, TARE, and systemic sponsors across most authors)
⚠️ No numeric detail on the allocation rules themselves in source: Figure 1 carries the system, and OCR captured no values

verdict.rationale: Consensus statement, not a trial. Diverges from BCLC by elevating EBRT/TARE to allocation-level options; reader needs to know the framework is contested.
verdict.audience: HCC across stages, North American practice setting

studies.significance: EBRT is written into the allocation algorithm itself, not left as a salvage footnote, and the split is driven by intrahepatic burden and vascular invasion rather than BCLC stage. That is the change: a rad onc gets a documented consensus basis for treating macrovascular invasion or bulky intrahepatic disease. No dose, fractionation, or target-volume guidance is in the source text.
studies.monday_clinic: In HCC with vascular invasion or bulky intrahepatic burden, where BCLC 2025 would route straight to systemic therapy, this supports a documented multidisciplinary basis for considering EBRT or TARE; it does not establish comparative outcomes against systemic therapy in that population.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Modified Delphi consensus** with a 20-member multidisciplinary North American panel spanning hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology, and radiation oncology. Framework built from current evidence plus expert opinion through iterative discussion and voting.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: In a **29-case pilot**, external expert treatment decisions were **96.6% concordant** with BEACON-HCC and **72.4% concordant** with BCLC 2025.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **EBRT** is named as a key incorporated modality alongside **TARE** and systemic-locoregional combinations. The source text gives no dose, fractionation, target volume, or patient-selection threshold for the RT recommendation.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents HCC treatment allocation in contemporary North American multidisciplinary practice. Does not represent settings where transplant, TARE, or EBRT access differs, nor does it carry outcome data for any allocation it recommends.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Concordance was measured against expert opinion, not survival, so a **higher concordance rate is agreement, not accuracy**, and the panel authored the framework it was scored against. Prospective validation is stated as planned through the HCC-Live Consortium.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: EBRT sits inside the allocation algorithm rather than as salvage, with tumor burden and vascular invasion as the branch points, giving a documented consensus basis for treating macrovascular invasion or bulky intrahepatic disease. Dose, fractionation, and target volume are not specified in source text.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Systemic-locoregional combination therapy is an allocation category, not an afterthought, so the sequencing question moves upstream to the tumor board rather than starting after locoregional failure. Vascular invasion and adverse prognostic markers, not BCLC stage alone, gate the systemic recommendation.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Allocation is keyed to intrahepatic burden and vascular invasion rather than BCLC stage, which affects who stays a resection or transplant candidate at the margins. The framework's stated aim is aligning allocation with tumor biology and therapeutic potential, not stage boundaries.

open_questions: Does BEACON-HCC allocation improve survival vs BCLC?
Which HCC patients benefit from EBRT vs TARE?

papers.title: BEACON-HCC: Best evidence and north american consensus on treatment allocation for hepatocellular carcinoma
authors: on behalf of HCC-Live Steering Committee
papers.abstract: Background : Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. Optimal treatment decisions are challenging, and existing treatment allocation frameworks may not fully reflect the evolving therapeutic landscape or contemporary clinical practices in North America. Methods : Using a modified Delphi process, a multidisciplinary panel of 20 North American experts in hepatology, medical oncology, surgery, radiology, and radiation oncology developed a consensus-based treatment framework for HCC, termed the BEACON-HCC system. The framework was informed by current evidence and expert opinion through iterative discussion and voting. In a pilot study using 29 real-world patient cases, we assessed concordance between external expert recommendations and BEACON-HCC recommendations and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) 2025 treatment recommendations. Results : The BEACON-HCC treatment allocation framework diverges from prior frameworks by incorporating nuanced clinical features such as degree of intrahepatic tumor burden and vascular invasion, and adverse tumor prognostic markers, to align treatment allocation with tumor biology and therapeutic potential. Key innovations include the incorporation of emerging modalities such as external beam radiation therapy (EBRT), transarterial radioembolization (TARE), and systemic-locoregional combination therapies. In the pilot exercise, expert treatment decisions showed 96.6% concordance with BEACON-HCC recommendations and 72.4% concordance with BCLC recommendations. Conclusions : BEACON-HCC is a consensus-based framework for treatment allocation that incorporates the expanding range of therapeutic options available to patients in the North American HCC population. Expert treatment decisions showed a high concordance with the BEACON-HCC system; further validation using empiric clinical data is planned through the HCC-Live Consortium.
